attributes.residual: REDUCED TO ONE OPCODE ROW WITH A PROVEN TWO-SIDED CONSTRAINT - this is the resolution stamp, and it is a genuine dead end by measurement rather than by budget. Baseline real 232, insns 244/244, multiset 2t; regnorm's prior screen found exactly 1 STRUCTURAL row over 252 paired instructions, so the 232 real lines are one systematic register-renaming permutation plus this row. THE ROW: +0x230 target `slwi r17,r18,3` vs ours `rlwinm r17,r18,3,13,28`, i.e. the target shifts the palette index unmasked and we mask it to 16 bits. SOURCE SITE FOUND: src/game/movie/movieplayer.c:609 `u16 val;`, built at :612-614 as `val = *ip; val |= ((bits >> nb) & 1) << 8;` (a 9-bit value) and consumed at :615 as `entry = pal + val * 8`. THE CONSTRAINT, measured in both directions: the u16 declaration is what makes MWCC emit the target's read-modify-write insert idiom at +0x228/+0x22c (`addi r18,r19,0` then `rlwimi r18,r17,8,23,23`, whose single-bit mask 23,23 also absorbs the source's `& 1`), and it is ALSO what makes MWCC's narrow-range analysis attach the 16-bit mask to the shift at +0x230. Widening the declaration to u32 and to int BOTH produced the identical result - `slwi` restored, but the insert lost, degrading to `rlwinm`+`or` (multiset 4t, real 232 -> 234). Two identical A/Bs kill the widening axis. The target holds BOTH halves simultaneously, so no single declared width for this variable reproduces it. AXES ALSO KILLED, both NEUTRAL: routing the shift through a separate u32 temp (`idx = val; entry = pal + idx * 8;`) - the u16 range propagates through the copy; and respelling `val * 8` as `(val << 3)`. NEXT HONEST MOVE, not attempted here: this TU is genuinely C++ (its own header says MoviePlayer.cpp, assert string at 0x80117684) compiled as .c with cflags_demo, so the C++ front end's integer-promotion and bitfield handling may resolve the two-sided constraint for free; fold this into the queued movieplayer .cpp conversion rather than probing the declaration again.
